subject: Weekly Revision
summary: a mixed revision of this week: machine tools, NTM and additive manufacturing (taper turning, milling, SLS), metrology and CIM (CNC constant surface speed, GD&T, CAPP), probability and statistics (geometric and normal distributions, regression lines), production planning and inventory (EOQ, moving averages, SPT) and operations research (AOA networks, M/M/1 queues, shadow prices)

questions.text: The short taper shown (from Ø60 mm to Ø50 mm over a length of 40 mm) is to be turned on a centre lathe by swivelling the compound rest. The angle (in degrees) through which the compound rest must be swivelled (round off to two decimal places) is ______
solution: Concept: The compound rest is set to the half taper angle α, where tan α = (D − d)/(2L).
Exam tip: The compound-rest method suits short, steep tapers (hand feed); long, gentle tapers are turned by tailstock set-over or a taper-turning attachment.

questions.text: Which one of the following additive manufacturing processes fuses a bed of polymer powder layer by layer with a laser beam?
opts: Stereolithography (SLA)
Fused deposition modelling (FDM)
Selective laser sintering (SLS)
Laminated object manufacturing (LOM)
solution: Concept: AM processes are grouped by the starting material: liquid (SLA: UV laser cures a photopolymer), solid filament/sheet (FDM extrudes, LOM cuts and bonds sheets) and powder (SLS, SLM, binder jetting).
A laser sintering a powder bed is SLS (C); the unsintered powder supports the part, so no support structures are needed.
Exam tip: SLM/DMLS fully melts metal powder; SLS normally sinters polymers such as nylon.

questions.text: Compared with up (conventional) milling, down (climb) milling
opts: requires a backlash eliminator in the table feed screw because the cutter tends to pull the work into itself
starts each cut at zero chip thickness, causing rubbing
tends to lift the workpiece off the table
is preferred for castings with hard, sandy skin
questions.ans: (A) requires a backlash eliminator in the table feed screw because the cutter tends to pull the work into itself
solution: Concept: In down milling the cutter rotates in the direction of the feed; each tooth enters at maximum chip thickness and exits at zero.
The cutting force pushes the work down onto the table and also in the feed direction, so any backlash in the lead screw lets the table jerk forward: a backlash eliminator is needed: (A)
Up milling starts at zero thickness (rubbing, poorer finish) and tends to lift the work, but it is used for hard-skinned castings.
Exam tip: Down milling gives better finish and longer tool life on rigid CNC machines with ball screws.

questions.text: A CNC lathe program uses G96 S180 (constant surface speed of 180 m/min). The spindle speed (in rpm) when the tool is cutting at a diameter of 40 mm (round off to one decimal place) is ______
solution: Concept: With constant surface speed (G96), the control changes the spindle speed as the diameter changes: N = 1000V/(πD).
Exam tip: In facing towards the centre N rises sharply, so G50 (or G92) S… is used to clamp the maximum spindle speed; G97 cancels CSS.

questions.text: Which one of the following geometric tolerances is always specified with respect to a datum?
opts: Flatness
Straightness
Circularity (roundness)
Position
solution: Concept: Form tolerances (flatness, straightness, circularity, cylindricity) control a feature by itself and never use a datum.
Orientation (parallelism, perpendicularity, angularity), location (position, concentricity, symmetry) and run-out tolerances relate a feature to a datum: (D)
Exam tip: Profile of a line/surface may be used with or without a datum.

questions.text: In computer-aided process planning (CAPP), the variant (retrieval) approach
opts: creates every process plan from scratch using decision logic and a manufacturing database
retrieves the standard plan of the part family (found by group-technology coding) and edits it for the new part
needs no part classification or coding
is used only for assembly planning
questions.ans: (B) retrieves the standard plan of the part family (found by group-technology coding) and edits it for the new part
solution: Concept: CAPP has two approaches: variant and generative.
Variant: code the new part (GT), find its family, retrieve the family's standard plan and modify it: (B)
Generative: synthesises a new plan from part geometry, decision rules and process knowledge, with no stored family plan.
Exam tip: Variant systems are easier to build; generative systems are more consistent and need no existing plans.

questions.text: A fair die is thrown repeatedly until a six appears. The probability that more than four throws are needed (round off to three decimal places) is ______
solution: Concept: More than k throws are needed exactly when the first k throws all fail: P(N > k) = (1 − p)k.
Exam tip: The expected number of throws is 1/p = 6 (geometric distribution, which is memoryless).

questions.text: The lengths of rods are normally distributed with mean 50 mm and standard deviation 4 mm. Given Φ(1) = 0.8413 and Φ(0.5) = 0.6915, the probability that a rod lies between 48 mm and 54 mm (round off to three decimal places) is ______
solution: Concept: Standardise: z = (x − μ)/σ, and use Φ(−z) = 1 − Φ(z).
Exam tip: Sketch the bell curve and shade the area; it avoids sign errors with negative z.

questions.text: If the correlation coefficient between x and y is zero, the two regression lines (y on x and x on y)
opts: coincide
are parallel
are perpendicular to each other, parallel to the coordinate axes
make an angle of 45° with each other
questions.ans: (C) are perpendicular to each other, parallel to the coordinate axes
solution: Concept: The regression lines are y − ȳ = r(σy/σx)(x − x̄) and x − x̄ = r(σx/σy)(y − ȳ).
With r = 0 they become y = ȳ (horizontal) and x = x̄ (vertical): perpendicular: (C)
With r = ±1 they coincide.
Exam tip: Both regression lines always pass through (x̄, ȳ).

questions.text: The annual demand of an item is 7200 units, the ordering cost is ₹250 per order and the holding cost is ₹10 per unit per year. Under the EOQ policy, the number of orders placed per year is ______
solution: Concept: EOQ = √(2DCo/Ch); number of orders = D/EOQ.
Orders per year = 7200/600 = 12
Exam tip: Directly, N* = √(DCh/(2Co)) = √(7200 × 10/500) = 12.

questions.text: Increasing the number of periods n in a simple moving-average forecast
opts: makes the forecast respond faster to a change in demand
makes the forecast smoother but slower to respond to a real change in demand
gives more weight to the latest demand
has no effect on the lag of the forecast
questions.ans: (B) makes the forecast smoother but slower to respond to a real change in demand
solution: Concept: A simple moving average gives equal weight 1/n to each of the last n periods.
Larger n averages out random noise (smoother) but the forecast lags a trend or step change by about (n − 1)/2 periods: (B)
Exam tip: A moving average of n periods behaves roughly like exponential smoothing with α = 2/(n + 1).

questions.text: Five jobs with processing times of 5, 3, 8, 2 and 7 hours wait for a single machine and are sequenced by the SPT rule. The average number of jobs in the system over the makespan (round off to two decimal places) is ______
solution: Concept: Average number of jobs in the system = (sum of completion times)/(makespan), since each job stays in the system until it completes.
SPT order: 2, 3, 5, 7, 8 → completion times 2, 5, 10, 17, 25 (sum = 59)
Average number in system = 59/25 = 2.36
Exam tip: Because the makespan is fixed, SPT, which minimises the sum of completion times, also minimises the average work-in-process.

questions.text: In an activity-on-arrow project network, a dummy activity is used to
opts: show a correct precedence relationship or to keep two activities between the same pair of events distinct; it takes zero time and no resources
represent an activity that is not on the critical path
represent waiting time that consumes resources
reduce the project duration by crashing
questions.ans: (A) show a correct precedence relationship or to keep two activities between the same pair of events distinct; it takes zero time and no resources
solution: Concept: In AOA networks each activity is an arrow between two events, and no two activities may share both end events.
A dummy (dashed arrow, zero duration, no resources) keeps parallel activities uniquely numbered and models logic that cannot be drawn otherwise: (A)
Exam tip: Activity-on-node networks need no dummies; that is one reason they are preferred in software.

questions.text: In an M/M/1 queue, the arrival rate is 4 per hour and the service rate is 5 per hour. The average number of customers waiting in the queue (excluding the one being served) is ______
solution: Concept: Lq = λ²/[μ(μ − λ)] = ρ²/(1 − ρ).
Lq = 0.64/0.2 = 3.2 customers (L = ρ/(1 − ρ) = 4)
Exam tip: Wq = Lq/λ = 0.8 h by Little's law.

questions.text: In the optimal simplex table of a maximisation LP, the shadow price (dual value) of a resource constraint means
opts: the cost of buying one unit of the resource in the market
the number of units of the resource left unused
the reduced cost of a non-basic variable
the increase in the optimal objective value per unit increase in the availability of that resource, within the range of feasibility
questions.ans: (D) the increase in the optimal objective value per unit increase in the availability of that resource, within the range of feasibility
solution: Concept: The optimal dual variable yi = ∂Z*/∂bi; it is read from the net-evaluation row under the slack of constraint i.
It is the marginal worth of one more unit of the resource, valid while the current basis stays feasible: (D)
A resource with unused slack (non-binding constraint) has a shadow price of zero (complementary slackness).
Exam tip: Buy extra resource only if its market price is below its shadow price.
